newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude prices soft ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude prices soft ahead of holiday.

text.p: The U.S. West Coast crude market was inactive Thursday, though traders said they expected prices to weaken after a long holiday weekend.
Local benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) was being offered by dominant seller BP Oil at 90 cents below West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, while buyers were holding out for more than $1.00 below.
The last confirmed deal was on March 13 at 91 cents below WTI, with small pieces subsquently traded privately.
"ANS is widening; that is the trend," said a trader at a company which buys and sells the Alaskan grade.
